rationale: Across the definitive cohort describing Cornelia de Lange syndrome 7 (CdLS7) caused by pathogenic MAU2 variants (18 individuals carrying 15 heterozygous variants), short stature and microcephaly constitute the hallmark clinical features, spanning classic craniofacial dysmorphism to milder presentations without severe structural transverse limb reduction defects (such as oligodactyly, forearm aplasia, or absence of the ulna/radius). In contrast to classic CdLS (primarily driven by NIPBL variants), where severe upper-limb reduction anomalies occur in roughly 25% of affected individuals, individuals with disruptions affecting the MAU2 cohesin loader subunit do not present with severe structural limb reductions (0/18 in the primary MAU2 series). Consequently, the presence of severe structural limb reduction defects yields a very low diagnostic likelihood of MAU2-related CdLS (CdLS7).

evidence.text: Characterization of 18 individuals with 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants established that affected individuals display phenotypes ranging from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly identified as the consistent primary features, without severe structural transverse limb reduction deficiencies.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of minor digital anomalies (such as fifth-finger clinodactyly or subtle brachydactyly) in expanded MAU2 patient cohorts compared to classic NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: While severe structural limb reductions (absent forearms/oligodactyly) appear to be absent in MAU2 variants, determining whether minor digit anomalies occur at high frequency would refine the clinical scoring algorithm for CdLS7.

new_directions.question_text: How do MAU2 truncating versus in-frame variants differentiate in craniofacial severity score and growth restriction?
new_directions.rationale: De Polli Cellin et al. noted two distinct episignatures corresponding to in-frame variants impairing NIPBL interaction versus truncating variants causing haploinsufficiency, which may correlate with distinct phenotypic sub-clusters.
